items.title: Abbie Williams Interview, 1966-06-02
items.q: The interviewer states 'And what's your name? Paul Crawford.' The interviewee does not respond to this identification with any personal connection or recognition, merely continuing the biographical narrative.

ctx.x: No, I could never get that coat back. He kept that coat, it was a blue shirt and suit I had bought at Mark's Isaac and he never was giving my coat back. I guess look now, he could buy me a hundred coats right now. I want him to have a coat and a tie on, like the rest of us, you see. I used him on piano. He used to be some scared to work with him. He wouldn't have been for Harrison Braden, his brother-in-law, Barrett. He wouldn't have made that job, you

know? So he brought him on up. Let's start off at the beginning, if we can. Let's get your name down. My name, Abby Williams. That's your father? A-B-E-I-E. We'll get that straight. And what's your name? Paul Crawford. And mine is Dick Allen. Can we start at the very beginning of your life, when you were born and where?

Yeah, you want to start now. Born here in New Orleans, 1906 September 22nd. Raised in New Orleans. Raised in New Orleans. What's that? Right here. Down Philly Shandris Street. Which? Philly Shandris. Down the night war. That's what I was born at. Did you hear much music around the house, your family play around the house? Oh wow, I follow the, I like it. I follow the music and drums. Drums were really my, drum was really my, my praise. Sticking. Sticking. Sticking. Sticking. Sticking.
